title: DNS Resolution
definition: The Domain Name System (DNS) translates human-readable domain names (like google.com) into machine-readable IP addresses (like 142.250.190.46). It is highly distributed and hierarchical.
simpleExplanation: DNS is the phonebook of the internet. You look up a name ('Google'), and DNS gives you the phone number ('IP Address') so your computer can connect.
diagramContent:
sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser
  participant OS as OS Cache
  participant ISP as ISP Resolver
  participant Root as Root Server
  participant TLD as TLD Server
  participant Auth as Authoritative Server
  B->>OS: Check cache for 'google.com'
  OS-->>B: Miss
  B->>ISP: What is 'google.com'?
  ISP->>Root: Where is '.com'?
  Root-->>ISP: Go to TLD Server
  ISP->>TLD: Where is 'google.com'?
  TLD-->>ISP: Go to Auth Server
  ISP->>Auth: What is 'google.com' IP?
  Auth-->>ISP: 142.250.190.46
  ISP-->>B: 142.250.190.46

answers.question: Define DNS Resolution.
answers.answer: DNS Resolution is a core mechanism in frontend architectures.

answers.question: What is the main bottleneck for DNS Resolution?
answers.answer: Usually network latency or CPU-bound synchronous tasks blocking the main thread.
